content.user_title: Improve Testing with TDD and E2E Strategy
content.value_statement: Teams often ship code without clear proof that behavior works. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through TDD, integration tests, and Playwright E2E checks.
actual_capabilities: Guides a red, green, refactor workflow for feature work.
Encourages writing a failing test before production code.
Promotes tests against real implementations instead of broad mocks.
Suggests integration testing with real databases or MSW.
Frames Playwright E2E tests around complete user flows.
Provides a checklist for coverage and test order.
limitations: It provides strategy and examples, not a complete test framework.
It does not choose project-specific tooling without repository context.
It cannot guarantee full coverage without existing product requirements.
It may need adaptation for legacy systems with heavy mocking.

use_cases.title: Plan Feature Tests
use_cases.description: Create a failing test plan before implementing a new feature.

use_cases.title: Reduce Mock Reliance
use_cases.description: Replace broad mocks with real implementations, test databases, or MSW boundaries.

use_cases.title: Validate User Journeys
use_cases.description: Add Playwright checks for checkout, signup, and other critical flows.

prompt_templates.title: Start TDD for a Feature
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the testing-strategy skill. Help me write the first failing test for this feature before production code.

prompt_templates.title: Design Integration Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the testing-strategy skill. Review this feature and propose integration tests that use real implementations where practical.

prompt_templates.title: Replace Fragile Mocks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the testing-strategy skill. Identify broad mocks in these tests and suggest real or MSW-backed alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Full Release Test Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the testing-strategy skill. Create a release test plan with TDD units, integration checks, and Playwright E2E flows.

output_examples.input: I need to add checkout discounts.
output: A failing discount calculation test comes first.
Integration coverage should use the real pricing module.
A Playwright flow should confirm the discounted total appears at checkout.

output_examples.input: Our API tests mock the database and client.
output: Keep mocks only at external service boundaries.
Use a test database for persistence behavior.
Use MSW for HTTP behavior that must stay controlled.

output_examples.input: Prepare tests before a signup release.
output: Unit tests cover validation rules first.
Integration tests cover account creation and email handoff.
E2E tests cover the complete signup path from browser to confirmation.

best_practices: Write the smallest failing test before production changes.
Prefer real implementations for behavior that the product owns.
Use E2E tests for critical user journeys, not every small branch.
anti_patterns: Writing production code first and adding tests only after review.
Mocking owned modules so tests no longer verify real behavior.
Using E2E tests as the only safety net for all logic.

faq.question: Does this skill require a specific test runner?
faq.answer: No. It mentions Vitest, Jest, and Playwright, but the workflow can fit other tools.

faq.question: Does the skill ban all mocks?
faq.answer: No. It discourages broad mocks of owned code and allows controlled HTTP boundaries with MSW.

faq.question: Can it help with legacy test suites?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it to identify high-value areas where real implementation tests can replace fragile mocks.

faq.question: Is this a security testing skill?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on software behavior, regression prevention, and release confidence.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it during implementation?
faq.answer: Yes. The prompts guide AI coding tools to test first, implement second, and refactor after passing tests.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect test plans, test sequencing, coverage advice, and E2E scenario suggestions.
